scenes.line1: Why is Ansible a favorite for automation?
scenes.say: Why do engineers trust Ansible for automating tasks across fleets? What makes it so reliable?

scenes.label: Agentless
scenes.sub: No agent needed—runs over SSH or WinRM.
scenes.say: Ansible is agentless. It connects directly to machines using SSH or WinRM, so you don't need to install anything extra.
It's perfect for patching, setting baselines, and managing users across a fleet. You get consistent results every time.

scenes.title: Install chrony & secure SSH
scenes.say: You write playbooks in YAML. Here, we install chrony and lock down root logins. The check option lets you dry run changes before applying.

scenes.question: What does idempotent mean in Ansible?
scenes.wrong: It runs faster than other tools.
scenes.right: Running it once or ten times leaves the system in the same state.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: What does idempotent mean in Ansible? It's not about speed—it's about always ending up in the same state, no matter how many times you run it.
